writeup.headline: IBIT rates Hold at 45, one point above Sell, on weak 12-month momentum and neutral news.
writeup.thesis: IBIT is a bitcoin trust, so the usual growth, quality, balance sheet and valuation factors have no data, and the score of 45 rests only on trend (39) and news risk (50), weighted equally. The trend score is held down by shares down 27.5% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and a price 28.4% below its 52-week high, plus shares 1.1 pp behind SPY and 2.0 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days. Shorter-term signals are firmer, with the price 0.9% above its 50-day average and 11.0% above its 200-day average. News is neutral across all six topics: no guidance, no fund-specific analyst actions or litigation, an unchanged 0.25% sponsor fee, and mixed October flows. With the score sitting right on the Hold edge, the rating is fragile.
key_risks: The fund tracks bitcoin, so its price can swing sharply with the underlying asset.
Weak 12-month momentum: shares down 27.5% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and price 28.4% below its 52-week high.
Lower-fee rival bitcoin ETFs could draw assets if fee pressure returns.
Fund flows were mixed in October, with modest net outflows across the category.
Regulatory shifts around crypto products, such as SEC procedural changes, could affect the category.
what_would_change: A drop of just 1 point in the score, such as a weaker trend score from renewed price declines, would move the rating to Sell.
Moving up to Buy would need 20 more points, which would take a sustained rebound in momentum and relative strength against SPY and QQQ.
Clearly negative news, such as regulatory action or new fee pressure on IBIT, would lower the news risk score and likely push the rating to Sell.
Positive fund-specific developments, such as strong sustained inflows, could lift the news score toward the Buy band.
